newsitem.title: TURKEY: New Turkish govt cancels public cash pool system.
newsitem.headline: New Turkish govt cancels public cash pool system.

text.p: Turkey's new Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz cancelled a system introduced by the former government to pool all public revenues under a central cash management system.

In a circular released by Yilmaz, public enterprises whose Turkish lira and foreign currency accounts were included in the cash pool system were allowed to open their separate accounts at leading state Ziraat Bank.
Previously, the state enterprises were required to keep all their currency and lira accounts at four leading state banks.

"All Turkish lira and foreign exchange savings accounts kept at other state banks (Emlakbank, Halk Bank and Vakiflar bank) and private finance institutions will be transferred to Ziraat Bank in three months and all investment instruments will also be transferred to Ziraat Bank at maturity," the circular signed by Yilmaz said.
It said the state enterprises could freely determine the types and maturities of their accounts as well as interest rates on them through negotiations with Ziraat Bank, in line with market practices.

The regulation to pool all public revenues had gone into effect on November 1, 1996 to increase control of state funds. More than 1,000 trillion lira had accumulated in the cash pool accounts by the middle of March 1997.
